title: SRE Standards: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity, and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood Inference's SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning practices, reliability initiatives, incident review requirements, operational tooling recommendations, and runbook structure. It is intended for service owners, product managers, on-call engineers, and SREs who operate production services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane, and internal infra).

Goals:
- Provide a single, consistent approach to defining SLOs and error budgets across services.
- Describe capacity planning cadence and targets for elastic and reserved resources.
- Standardize incident review and postmortem practices to accelerate learning.
- Define minimal runbook coverage and runbook run cadence.
- Recommend operational tooling and dashboards required for SLO observability and capacity decisions.

1) SLO & Error Budget Standards

Intro and scope:
- SLOs should be defined for user-facing customer experience and internal critical flows (examples: API request latency p99, request success rate, model-generation availability, embedding pipeline throughput).
- Each service must have at least one Availability SLO and one Latency SLO, plus up to two domain-specific SLOs (e.g., model-serve-accuracy, cache-hit-rate).

SLO definitions (required fields):
- SLO name (short): e.g., api.request_latency.p99_ms
- Owner: team/service owner
- Target: numeric target and window (e.g., 99th percentile latency < 350ms over a 30-day rolling window)
- Measurement source: metric name and Prometheus/Grafana dashboard link or tracing query
- Alerting policy: who to page and on-call runbook link
- Error budget policy: burn thresholds and remedial actions

Example SLOs (recommended defaults):
- Availability: api.request_success_rate >= 99.95% (30d rolling)
- Latency: api.request_latency.p95 < 120ms; api.request_latency.p99 < 350ms (30d rolling)
- Streaming responses: stream.connect_success_rate >= 99.9% (30d)

Error budget burn policy (standardized):
- Green: burn < 10% of budget in a 7-day window — normal ops, standard changes allowed.
- Yellow: burn 10%–30% in 7 days — cap feature rollouts, apply mitigations, notify leadership.
- Red: burn > 30% in 7 days or >50% in 30 days — freeze new launches, run accelerated investigation, require mitigation plan and executive review.

Error budget response playbook (on-call steps):
1. Verify SLO alert and scope of impact (customer segment, region, model variant).
2. Triage root cause using dashboards and traces.
3. Apply short-term mitigation (increase capacity, fallback model variant, enable degraded mode).
4. Notify stakeholders (support, sales, customer success) if customers are impacted.
5. Open a postmortem and track error budget consumption until restored.

2) Capacity Planning

Principles:
- Capacity planning must balance latency SLOs, cost targets, and burstability for traffic spikes.
- Split capacity planning into Reserved (Dedicated) vs. Elastic (hosted autoscaling). Different processes apply.

Cadence:
- Quarterly capacity review (capacity planning meeting) with capacity owners, SRE, product, and finance.
- Monthly runway check: compute projected 30/60/90 day usage based on telemetry and active experiments.

Minimum artifacts required per service:
| Artifact | Owner | Update cadence | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Traffic forecast (Q30/60/90) | Service owner | Monthly | From traffic growth, product roadmap, marketing events |
| SLA vs SLO mapping | Service owner | Quarterly | When customer SLAs exist, map to internal SLOs |
| Cost per qps / per-token | Finance + Infra | Quarterly | Helps trade off reserved vs elastic |
| Safe headroom policy | SRE | Quarterly | e.g., maintain 20% headroom for autoscaling groups |

Capacity targets and headroom guidance:
- Production pools should target 75% median utilization under baseline traffic and 85% peak utilization, with autoscaler targets set to avoid p99 latency regressions.
- For Dedicated customer pools (reserved GPUs), maintain a minimum 10% warm spare capacity to cover common failure modes.
- For model-serving nodes using KV cache, plan for warm-up windows (estimated 30–90 minutes depending on model size and traffic patterns).

Scenario runbooks (examples):
- Sudden 3x traffic spike: scale autoscaler target to aggressive mode, add ephemeral instances, enable KV prefix caching, throttle noncritical batch jobs.
- Model rollout causing throughput drop: rollback model variant, reduce max concurrent requests per replica, trigger follow-up regression test job.

3) Reliability Initiatives & Roadmap Integration

What qualifies as a reliability initiative:
- Any project that materially improves SLO attainment, reduces toil for on-call, or mitigates systemic capacity/failure modes. Examples: migrating to the new batching runtime, multi-region failover automation, quantified autoscaler improvements.

Prioritization criteria (ranked):
1. Direct SLO impact (high)
2. Reduction in on-call toil (medium)
3. Cost savings without SLO regression (medium)
4. Compliance/regulatory requirements (high)

Tracking and measurement:
- Each initiative must declare success metrics (SLO delta, MTTR reduction, cost per token delta) and roll out with canary measurements and guardrail tests.
- Use the reliability roadmap board to track initiatives and expose quarter-level outcomes at QBRs.

4) Incident Review & Postmortem Standards

When to write a postmortem:
- All Sev 1 and Sev 2 incidents impacting customer-facing SLOs must have a postmortem published within 7 calendar days.
- Sev 3 incidents are at the discretion of the on-call lead when they represent recurring or systemic issues.

Postmortem required sections (minimum):
- Summary and impact (customer visible impact, duration, affected customers/regions).
- Timeline of events with timestamps.
- Root cause analysis (include evidence: logs, traces, config diffs).
- Corrective actions (short-term and long-term) with owners and ETA.
- Error budget impact and follow-up decisions (e.g., rollout freeze).
- Learnings and action items (RCA biases, tests, runbook updates).

Postmortem review process:
1. Draft within 72 hours by incident lead.
2. Peer review by at least one SRE and one service owner.
3. Publish in confluence and link to related alert/incident.
4. Track action items in JIRA and verify closure in the next on-call rotation.

5) Runbooks (operational playbooks)

Runbook standard structure (required):
- Title and scope (what systems and symptoms this runbook covers).
- Pager triggers and severity mapping (what alerts map to which SLO impact).
- Immediate triage checklist (first 5 items an on-call should run).
- Mitigation steps (ordered list of actions).
- Rollback steps (if applicable).
- Post-incident actions link (postmortem template).
- Owner and last-tested date.

Mandatory runbook coverage per service:
- On-call runbook for paging symptoms (must exist and be tested in the last 90 days).
- Capacity-scaling runbook (autoscaler configuration, manual scale commands).
- Deployment rollback runbook (how to revert a model or API release).

Example runbook snippet (Triage for high p99 latency on API):
1. Check Grafana dashboard: p95, p99, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization.
2. Check logs for OOMs or GC spikes: kubectl logs or GPU node logs.
3. Confirm recent deploys in last 30 minutes (gitops/CI status).
4. If model latencies are the cause, switch traffic to previous model variant via the router: curl -X POST "https://platform/router/switch" -d '{"model":"model-v2"}'.
5. If resource constrained, increase pool size: terraform apply -var="pool_desired=12" or run autoscaler override.
6. Notify stakeholders and update incident channel with status.

Runbook testing and validation:
- Each runbook owner must run a tabletop/read-through annually and an automated test of core runbook steps (where feasible) every 90 days.
- Record last-tested date in the runbook page metadata.

6) Operational Tooling Recommendations

Core tooling (minimum stack):
- Metrics/Alerts: Prometheus + Grafana (service dashboards per SLO).
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry -> Tempo/Jaeger with sampling policies tuned for model-serving traces.
- Logging: ELK/Cloud logging with structured logs and retention aligned with incident review needs (90 days default).
- Incident management: PagerDuty (alerting) + Slack incident channels + statuspage for customer communications.
- Runbooks & Postmortems: Confluence templates + JIRA for action tracking.
- Capacity forecasting: internal capacity-dashboard (data fed from telemetry, cost reports, and bookings).

Observability configuration guidance:
- Tag all SLO-related metrics with service, region, model_variant, and customer_tier.
- Use sampling for traces but preserve 100% for errors and tail latency traces.
- Dashboards must include: SLO overview panel, error budget burn rate, top error classes, top latency contributors, capacity utilization by pool.

7) Ownership & Governance

Roles and responsibilities:
- Service owner: defines SLOs, owns capacity forecast, responsible for runbook completeness.
- SRE: validates SLO definitions, authors shared runbooks, leads incident response for cross-service incidents.
- On-call engineer: executes runbooks, triages incidents, creates postmortem drafts.
- Product/PM: informs capacity planning and product launches, approves reliability initiatives when budgeted.

Governance cadence:
- Weekly SRE office hours for runbook and postmortem reviews.
- Quarterly reliability review with leadership to approve major initiatives and capacity purchases.
- SLO re-evaluation annually or when product changes affect user experience significantly.

8) Related pages and templates
- Postmortem template: /confluence/eng-sre/postmortem-template (use for all Sev1/2 incidents).
- Runbook template: /confluence/eng-sre/runbook-template (required fields as above).
- Capacity planning board: /confluence/eng-sre/capacity-roadmap-board

Appendix A — Quick reference: SLO targets and actions
| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| Error budget burn > 10% in 7d | Pause non-essential launches; investigate root cause |
| Error budget burn > 30% in 7d | Freeze releases, escalate to Head of SRE, mandatory mitigation plan |
| p99 latency > target for >1 hour | Follow high-p99 runbook; consider temporary traffic shaping |
